'''Moti Gitik''' ({{Langx|he|מוטי גיטיק}}) is a mathematician, working in [[set theory]], who is professor at the [[Tel-Aviv University]]. He was an [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker]] at the 2002 [[International Congresses of Mathematicians]], and became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2012.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-19.</ref>

==Research==
Gitik proved the [[relative consistency|consistency]] of "all uncountable cardinals are [[singular cardinal|singular]]" (a strong negation of the [[axiom of choice]]) from the consistency of "there is a proper class of [[strongly compact cardinal]]s". He further proved the [[equiconsistency]] of the following statements: 
* There is a cardinal ''κ'' with [[Mitchell order]] ''κ''<sup>++</sup>.
* There is a [[measurable cardinal]] ''κ'' with 2<sup>''κ''</sup> > ''κ''<sup>+</sup>.
* There is a [[strong limit cardinal|strong limit]] [[singular cardinal]] ''λ'' with 2<sup>''λ''</sup> > ''λ''<sup>+</sup>.
* The [[Continuum Hypothesis|GCH]] holds below ℵ<sub>ω</sub>, and 2<sup>ℵ<sub>ω</sub></sup>=ℵ<sub>ω+2</sub>.
Gitik discovered several methods for building models of ZFC with complicated Cardinal Arithmetic structure. His main results deal with consistency and equi-consistency of non-trivial patterns of the Power Function over singular cardinals.
